classification.difficultyReason: Part b requires interpreting equal-edge and right-angle markings to classify the four faces, constructing separate altitudes for two isosceles faces, and deriving the shared height of the two right-triangle faces.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of these solids. Round your answer to 1 d.p. where appropriate.

spec.description: Unshaded triangular pyramid with all six edges, dashed rear base edge, right-angle marks at the lower-left and front vertices, and the three supplied lengths. The model uses perpendicular lengths 5, 12 and 9.
spec.mathematics: The two missing face legs are sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13 and sqrt(12^2+9^2)=15. All four faces are right-angled triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and marks are visible.

answer.worked:
The two missing lengths needed for the face areas are
$$\begin{align*}d_1^2&=5^2+12^2\\d_1&=13\text{ cm}\\d_2^2&=12^2+9^2\\d_2&=15\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
All four faces are right-angled triangles, so
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(5)(12)+\frac12(12)(9)+\frac12(13)(9)+\frac12(5)(15)\\A&=30+54+58.5+37.5\\A&=180\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded triangular pyramid with apex directly above the right base vertex. The rear base edge is dashed. Single ticks identify the two equal 20 m apex edges; double ticks identify the two equal 12 m base edges. The remaining base edge is 10 m. The right-angle cue indicates the perpendicular apex edge.
spec.mathematics: Base sides are 12, 12 and 10 m. The perpendicular height is sqrt(20^2-12^2)=16 m. The remaining lateral face has sides 20, 20 and 10 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, equality marks and right-angle cues are visible.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height is
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=20^2-12^2\\h&=16\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The altitude of the base bisects its $10\text{ m}$ side:
$$\begin{align*}b^2&=12^2-5^2\\b&=\sqrt{119}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The altitude of the face with sides $20$, $20$ and $10\text{ m}$ is
$$\begin{align*}s^2&=20^2-5^2\\s&=\sqrt{375}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The other two faces are right-angled triangles:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(10)\sqrt{119}+\frac12(10)\sqrt{375}+2\left(\frac12(12)(16)\right)\\A&=5\sqrt{119}+5\sqrt{375}+192\\A&\approx343.4\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
